results.title: Turkey: Steel plant explosion kills 17 in Izmir province
results.content: A devastating explosion at the Habaş iron and steelworks in Aliağa, in western Turkey has killed 17 people. Witnesses described an earthquake-like blast, while footage shows flames, thick smoke and distressed relatives outside the factory.

results.title: Poland: Tusk and Nawrocki honour six victims of Kraków shooting
results.content: Poland's President and Prime Minister set aside their political differences to honour the six victims of a deadly shooting in Kraków. The two leaders laid candles and knelt together at a vigil in the historic city centre.

results.title: Turkey: Delegates arrive in Antalya as COP31 climate talks begin
results.content: The United Nations COP31 climate summit has opened in Antalya after a year marked by deadly heatwaves and devastating floods. Delegates face fresh challenges as the war in Iran disrupts global energy supplies.

results.title: French judo star Teddy Rinner announces run for presidency
results.content: Judy star Teddy Rinner wants to be the next president of France. The 37-year-old Olympic champion announced his bid on social media on Monday. The news comes as polls show the French public largely split between the far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melanchon and the far-right's Marine Le Pen.

results.title: South Africa: ANC Loses Ground, Coalition Talks Take Centre Stage [Africanews Today]
results.content: Nelson Mandela's party is losing ground, although it remains the country's largest political force.

results.title: Ethiopia: Reusable sanitary pads help girls break the silence around menstruation
results.content: In a country that imports all its sanitary pads, their high cost puts them beyond the reach of many women and girls. For those unable to afford them, periods can mean missed school days, lost income and, in some cases, resorting to unsafe alternatives.

results.title: Argentina: Pope Leo XIV receives warm welcome in Claypole
results.content: Pope Leo XIV was welcomed by crowds in Claypole, near Buenos Aires, as he visited the Don Orione care home. The pontiff greeted the faithful and unveiled a plaque during his 12-day South American tour.

results.title: Thousands of Ethiopian Jews mark holy day of Sigd in Jerusalem
results.content: Thousands of Ethiopian Jews gathered in Jersualem on Monday to mark the holy day of Sigd. Religious leaders known as Kessim led the community in prayer. Sigd is one of the few holidays unique to the Ethiopian Jewish community.

results.title: Kenyan authorities seize 454kg of crystal meth worth $27 million
results.content: Kenyan authorities have seized 454 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine worth $27 million in a multi-agency operation, the police said Monday.

results.title: Senegalese surfer uses the waves to give children hope
results.content: The country's hosting of the Youth Olympic Games is also shining a spotlight on its surfing potential, as the first Olympic event ever held on African soil brings global attention to Senegal.

results.title: Deadly train crash reignites calls for overhaul of Egypt's railway network
results.content: Sunday's deadly train crash that killed seven people and injured dozens more has reignited calls for an overhaul of Egypt's ageing railway system. The accident happened when a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum rear-ended another on the Cairo-Aswan route.

results.title: At least 39 killed in migrant boat sinking off Senegal
results.content: Regional governor Ndeye Nguenar Mbodj says four more bodies were found this morning, raising the death toll from 35. Twenty-three victims have been identified by their families.

results.title: Trump says "tough" US deportation policy may explain midterm losses
results.content: President Donald Trump in his first major interview since his party lost control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections said he thinks his administration was too aggressive on deportations and that he thinks he can work with Democrats in the new Congress on some kind of immigration deal.

results.title: Slave trade: Ghana's president says reparations not limited to cash payments
results.content: John Mahama specifically cited investments in education, health, economic growth and debt treatment as interventions that could be considered as reparations to redress historical wrongs

results.title: Egypt: Seven dead, 125 injured in collision between two trains
results.content: Rail workers began repairing damaged tracks in Al-Ayyat, Egypt, on Monday 9 November, a day after two passenger trains collided south of Cairo, killing seven people and injuring at least 125 others.

results.title: Kenya seizes $27m worth of methamphetamine in coastal drug raid
results.content: Kenyan police have confiscated 454 kilograms of methamphetamine valued at $27 million in a joint operation with Tanzanian authorities targeting cross-border drug trafficking.

results.title: Philippines: 'Trump out!' Women rally ahead of ASEAN summit
results.content: Women protesters took to the streets of Manila on Monday 9 November ahead of Donald Trump's visit for the 49th ASEAN summit. Carrying "Trump Out" placards, they also denounced a US-led initiative on semiconductors and critical minerals.

results.title: Sudan re-arrests former Bashir official wanted by ICC
results.content: Ahmed Haroun, a senior security official during the rule of longtime dictator Omar al-Bashir, and later chairman of the former ruling National Congress Party, was detained in Omdurman, the sister city of the capital, Khartoum, according to two lawyers on his defense team. results.title: ‘We are left with silence’: Egypt’s press freedom under threat
results.content: Egypt's latest prosecution of journalists attempts to "silence" the last surviving vestiges of the free press, Lina Attalah, head of preeminent outlet Mada Masr, told AFP days before she faces jail time in court.

results.title: Iranian citizens expect Israel’s Iran policy to remain unchanged
results.content: Iranians see no prospects of change to Israel's policy over Tehran even under a new Israeli government.

results.title: Senegal: Dakar surf school helps young Africans reclaim the waves
results.content: On the beaches of Dakar, a surf school is making the waves accessible to local children. Founder Ibra Samb, who learnt to surf on plywood, hopes to inspire a new generation.

results.title: 'People have spoken': Ramaphosa reacts to outcome of local govt polls
results.content: The African National Congress, which has dominated South African politics since the end of apartheid, took 30.76 percent of votes in municipal elections, its worst-ever electoral performance, the electoral commission said Sunday

results.title: Argentina: Pope Leo XIV welcomed by Javier Milei for historic visit
results.content: Pope Leo XIV has arrived in Argentina, on Sunday 8 November, for the first papal visit to the country in nearly 40 years. President Javier Milei welcomed him at Buenos Aires airport, while the city's iconic obelisk was illuminated in his honour.

results.title: Egypt train crash: Survivors describe horror after collision kills seven
results.content: Seven people were killed and at least 125 others injured when two trains collided Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, the Chief Prosecutor’s office said in a statement

results.title: Netherlands: Sea of red fills Amsterdam streets in Gaza protest
results.content: Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam in the Netherlands on Sunday 8 November, demanding that the Dutch government take stronger action against Israel over the war in Gaza.

results.title: Poland: Kraków mourns six victims as shooting site reopens
results.content: Kraków's historic main square in southern Poland reopened to the public on Sunday 8 November, just over 24 hours after a deadly shooting left six people dead and 15 others injured. Residents are lighting candles in memory of the victims, while bullet marks remain visible on café windows.

results.title: South Africa's ANC faces coalition talks after local election losses
results.content: The African National Congress came in first place in South Africa's local elections but suffered its worst-ever electoral setback, according to final results on Sunday.
